# AGENTS.md — design layer

This repository uses [modelroom](https://github.com/modelroom/modelroom): one room per screen,
with the reason, the invisible spec, the promises and the artifact kept apart.

You are working inside the design layer (`modelroom/`). Write the room's prose in English.

## Where you may write

- `rooms/<room>/BRIEF.md` — why this room exists
- `rooms/<room>/SPEC.md` — what the artifact cannot show (devices, states, constraints, what it may use)
- `rooms/<room>/BEHAVIOUR.md` — what it promises (operations and results)
- `rooms/<room>/index.html` — the artifact itself

`rooms/<room>/index.png` is the artifact's rendering: do not hand-edit it, produce
it with `{{cli}} render <room>` and commit it with the html.

A new room, a rename and a removal go through the CLI
(`{{cli}} add|rename|remove`), or the tool UI's add button and room menu —
the same code; the directory name is the room, and the references to it have to
move with it.

Nothing else. Do not reach outside this directory; the design layer never reads the
application code. The application is handed this layer, not the other way round.

## The layer's design rules

`DESIGN.md` holds what is shared across rooms — the tokens, the components, the
accessibility floor. A room takes from it and names what it took in its `SPEC.md`; it
does not invent a colour or a component that is already there. Change `DESIGN.md` only
when the decision is genuinely layer-wide — otherwise it belongs to the room.

A design system is shared too, and it is shared **once**: `vendor/<system>/` holds the
system's files (copied from the pinned package, committed) and `design.css` holds the
layer's own CSS. A room links both by relative path (`../../design.css`) — the same path
resolves when the artifact is rendered from disk and when it is served. Do not hand-edit
either file and do not install a framework inside a room; refreshing the copy is the
project's script. `DESIGN.md` names both, and the version the vendored copy was taken from.

It also names the design system's MCP server, when there is one. The server itself is
configured in `opencode.json`, which OpenCode reads from this layer; use its tools to
look components and tokens up before writing markup.

## How to work

1. Read the room's `BRIEF.md` first, then `SPEC.md` and `BEHAVIOUR.md`.
2. Change the artifact to match them. If they are wrong, say so — do not quietly reword them.
3. Keep the artifact self-contained: no CDN, no web fonts, no build step. It is going to be
   handed to implementation, so it must render with no network. Sharing is not the enemy of
   that — link `vendor/` and `design.css` relatively instead of fetching anything or copying
   a framework into the room.
4. Never restate in `SPEC.md` what can be seen in the artifact. Never copy a promise into
   two files; reference it by id (`@verb-1`) instead.
5. Promises that need the real system (records, timestamps, permissions) do not belong in
   this layer.
6. After changing `index.html`, run `{{cli}} render <room>` so `index.png` matches.
   The picture is what gets reviewed; a stale snapshot is worse than no commit.

## The picture is the deliverable

The room's reviewable output is the docs and the snapshot, not the markup. When a change
is meant to be invisible — an accessibility fix, a refactor that must not move a pixel —
`{{cli}} render <room> --check` proves the pixels are unchanged: it renders to a
temporary file and compares. A change that *is* meant to move the picture leaves a new
`index.png`, and the pull request shows it.

Three skills come with the layer, under `.agents/skills/`:

- `read-modelroom` — read the docs **and the picture** before changing the room.
- `create-modelroom-pr` — snapshot first, then open a PR carrying the image, the context
  and the BEHAVIOUR.
- `manage-modelroom-rooms` — create, rename or remove a room without leaving a broken
  reference behind.

The snapshot keeps a fixed name (`index.png`) and is overwritten in place, so GitHub can
diff it on the pull request. Merge with **Squash and Merge**: main keeps the final image
and git collects the intermediate ones.

## Conventions

- Frontmatter keys (`title`, `status`, `summary`, `tags`) and promise ids (`@verb-1`) stay
  in English, whatever language the prose uses.
- Add `status: draft|review|adopted` to `BRIEF.md` when you want the dashboard to show a
  state. Changing it to `adopted` is a human decision, not yours.
- If this room is not the project's default screen, say so with `device: <name>` in
  `BRIEF.md`. The names are `sp`, `tablet`, `pc`, plus whatever `modelroom.json` defines;
  the snapshot is rendered at that device.
- A room that is part of a flow names its application with `app: <name>` (free text —
  `user`, `admin`, `user-legacy`) and its one main next screen with `next: <room>`. The
  dashboard's app tabs and flow view are built from these; keep `next` inside its own `app`.
- A link from one room's screen to another is written **relative to the room**
  (`<a href="../top/index.html">`), so it resolves both when the artifact is opened from
  disk and when it is served. An absolute `/rooms/top/index.html` does not work.

See `docs/02-convention.md` in the modelroom package for the reasoning.

# AGENTS.md — デザインレイヤー

このリポジトリは [modelroom](https://github.com/modelroom/modelroom) を使っています。
1画面につき1つの room を作り、理由・見えない仕様・約束・artifact を分けて保ちます。

あなたはデザインレイヤー（`modelroom/`）の中で作業しています。room の文章は日本語で書いてください。

## 書き込んでよい場所

- `rooms/<room>/BRIEF.md` — この room が存在する理由
- `rooms/<room>/SPEC.md` — artifact では見えないこと（デバイス、状態、制約、使ってよいもの）
- `rooms/<room>/BEHAVIOUR.md` — 何を約束するか（操作と結果）
- `rooms/<room>/index.html` — artifact そのもの

`rooms/<room>/index.png` は artifact を描画したものです。手で編集せず、
`{{cli}} render <room>` で生成し、html と一緒にコミットします。

room の追加・改名・削除は CLI（`{{cli}} add|rename|remove`）、またはツール UI の
追加ボタンと room メニューで行います（同じコードです）。ディレクトリ名が room そのもので、
その room への参照も一緒に動かす必要があります。

それ以外は書き込まないでください。このディレクトリの外には出ないでください。
デザインレイヤーはアプリケーションのコードを読みません。アプリケーションに渡すのは
このレイヤーであり、その逆ではありません。

## レイヤーのデザインルール

`DESIGN.md` に、room をまたいで共有するものを置きます — トークン、コンポーネント、
アクセシビリティの下限です。room はそこから取り、取ったものを `SPEC.md` に書きます。
すでにある色やコンポーネントを room 側で作り直してはいけません。`DESIGN.md` を変えるのは、
判断が本当にレイヤー全体に及ぶときだけです — そうでなければその room に属します。

デザインシステムも共有するものですが、共有は**一度だけ**です。`vendor/<system>/` に
システムのファイル（固定したパッケージからコピーし、コミットしたもの）を、`design.css` に
レイヤー自身の CSS を置きます。room は両方を相対パス（`../../design.css`）で読み込みます —
artifact をディスクから描画するときも、配信されるときも同じパスで解決します。どちらの
ファイルも手で編集せず、room の中にフレームワークを入れてはいけません。コピーの更新は
プロジェクトのスクリプトが行います。`DESIGN.md` に両方と、ベンダリングしたコピーを
取り込んだバージョンを書きます。

デザインシステムの MCP サーバがある場合、それも `DESIGN.md` に書きます。サーバ自体の設定は
`opencode.json` で、OpenCode がこのレイヤーから読みます。マークアップを書く前に、そのツールで
コンポーネントとトークンを調べてください。

## 進め方

1. まず room の `BRIEF.md` を読み、次に `SPEC.md` と `BEHAVIOUR.md` を読みます。
2. それらに合うように artifact を変えます。仕様が間違っているなら、黙って書き換えず、
   間違っていると伝えてください。
3. artifact は自己完結にします。CDN、Webフォント、ビルド手順は使いません。実装に渡す
   ものなので、ネットワークなしで描画できる必要があります。共有することはそれと矛盾しません —
   何かを取得したりフレームワークを room にコピーしたりせず、`vendor/` と `design.css` を
   相対パスで読み込みます。
4. `SPEC.md` に、artifact を見れば分かることを書き直さないでください。同じ約束を2つの
   ファイルにコピーせず、id（`@verb-1`）で参照します。
5. 実際のシステムが必要とする約束（レコード、タイムスタンプ、権限）は、このレイヤーには
   置きません。
6. `index.html` を変えたら `{{cli}} render <room>` を実行し、`index.png` を一致
   させます。レビューされるのは画像です。古いスナップショットは、コミットしないより
   悪い状態です。

## 画像が成果物です

その room のレビュー対象は docs とスナップショットであり、マークアップではありません。
見た目を変えないはずの変更（アクセシビリティ対応、ピクセルを動かしてはいけない
リファクタ）では、`{{cli}} render <room> --check` がピクセル不変を証明します —
一時ファイルに描画して比較します。逆に、見た目を変える変更は新しい `index.png` を
残し、PR がそれを表示します。

このレイヤーには3つのスキルが `.agents/skills/` に付いてきます:

- `read-modelroom` — 変更の前に、docs **と画像**を読む。
- `create-modelroom-pr` — まずスナップショットを取り、画像・コンテキスト・BEHAVIOUR を
  載せた PR を作る。
- `manage-modelroom-rooms` — 参照を壊さずに room を作成・改名・削除する。

スナップショットは固定名（`index.png`）で、その場で上書きします。そうすることで
GitHub が PR で画像の差分を表示できます。マージは **Squash and Merge** で行います —
main には最終の1枚だけが残り、中間の画像は git が回収します。

## 決まりごと

- frontmatter のキー（`title`、`status`、`summary`、`tags`）と約束の id（`@verb-1`）は、
  文章がどの言語でも英語のままにします。
- ダッシュボードに状態を出したいときは、`BRIEF.md` に `status: draft|review|adopted` を
  足します。`adopted` に変えるのは人間の判断で、あなたの判断ではありません。
- この room がプロジェクトの既定の画面でない場合は、`BRIEF.md` に `device: <name>` を
  書きます。名前は `sp`、`tablet`、`pc` と、`modelroom.json` が定義したものです。
  スナップショットはそのデバイスで描画されます。
- フローの一部である room は、`app: <name>`（自由記述 — `user`、`admin`、`user-legacy`）で
  アプリケーションを、`next: <room>` で主要な次の画面を1つ書きます。ダッシュボードの
  app タブと flow ビューはこれらから作られます。`next` は同じ `app` の中で保ちます。
- room の画面から別の room の画面へのリンクは、**room からの相対パス**で書きます
  （`<a href="../top/index.html">`）。ディスクから開くときも配信されるときも同じパスで
  解決します。絶対パスの `/rooms/top/index.html` は動きません。

理由は modelroom パッケージの `docs/02-convention.md` にあります。

# Open a modelroom pull request

A reviewer reads the picture first. The image has to be in the commit and named
in the description, or the review is markup-only.

The png is committed under a **fixed name** (`index.png`) and overwritten in
place every time. That is deliberate: GitHub diffs two versions of the *same
path* with **Files changed → image diff (Swipe / Onion Skin)**. Never rename it
to add a timestamp or a version — that would turn every change into two
unrelated files.

## Steps

1. Bring the snapshot up to date. Idempotent: nothing is written when the png
   already matches the artifact.

   ```sh
   {{cli}} render <room>
   ```

2. Commit the room's changed files **together** — the docs, `index.html`, and
   `index.png`. Stage only that room; do not sweep in unrelated work.

   ```sh
   git add rooms/<room>
   ```

3. Build the description from the room, then add the diff context yourself:

   ```sh
   {{cli}} pr-body <room>
   ```

   It prints the summary, where the snapshot is, and the BEHAVIOUR. Add a short
   note of what the change is for and why.

   To show the image inline in the description instead of pointing at it, pass a
   URL that renders for the reviewer — the raw file on the branch:

   ```sh
   {{cli}} pr-body <room> --image-url \
     "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/rooms/<room>/index.png"
   ```

4. Create or update the pull request:

   ```sh
   gh pr create --title "<room>: <what changed>" --body-file -
   gh pr edit  --body-file -        # when the PR already exists
   ```

## Why the snapshot is committed and overwritten

- A checked-out repository shows every screen without running anything — no
  Playwright, no server.
- A fixed path is what makes the pull request's image diff work.
- The binary churn that would normally bloat the repository is bounded by
  merging with **Squash and Merge**: main keeps the final image, and git
  collects the intermediate blobs once the branch goes away.

Do not attach the image to a PR comment as base64 — GitHub caps a comment at
65,536 characters, and a screen is far larger than that.

# Manage modelroom rooms

A room is `rooms/<room>/` with the required docs and an artifact. **The directory
name is the room.** It must be unique, it must be a lowercase slug, and it must
carry every doc `modelroom.json` names.

Do not create, move or delete a room directory by hand. `mkdir`, `mv` and `rm`
leave the references behind; the CLI keeps the name and the links in step. The
tool UI's **Add room** button and a room header's pencil/⋯ menu run this same
code, when a person would rather click than type a command.

## Add a room

```sh
{{cli}} add <room> --title "Sign in"
```

Then write the room, `BRIEF.md` first, and finish with:

```sh
{{cli}} render <room>
{{cli}} check
```

## Rename a room

Look before you move:

```sh
{{cli}} rename <old> <new> --dry-run
```

The dry run prints the directory move and every reference it would rewrite. Run
it again without `--dry-run` to do it. The CLI rewrites what is a reference — the
`superseded_by` frontmatter, the `/rooms/<name>` and `/files/<rooms>/<name>`
paths, relative links — and lists the places that still mention the old name.

Then finish what it cannot do:

1. Read every listed mention and decide whether it should change.
2. A `title` and an H1 are prose, not paths: the directory name and the name on
   the screen are allowed to differ. Change them only if the screen really
   renames.
3. `{{cli}} check`, then `{{cli}} render <room>`, then read
   `git diff` for what the script could not see.

Stop `{{cli}}` first. The running server holds the room's chat session in
memory, and a rename underneath it loses that; the command refuses while a server
is up.

## Remove a room

Removal is a human decision. An agent retires a room instead:

```yaml
deprecated: true
superseded_by: <the room that replaced it>
```

Only when the person has clearly asked to delete it:

```sh
{{cli}} remove <room> --dry-run   # who still points at it?
{{cli}} remove <room> --yes
```

`remove` refuses while another room points at it, unless you pass `--force`; a
forced removal leaves those references broken, so fix them. There is no undo
beyond git — commit the removal on its own so it can be reverted.

## Refresh the layer's generated files

The skills and `AGENTS.md` are generated from the installed modelroom, so a new
version can change them:

```sh
{{cliLatest}} update            # refresh the generated files
{{cliLatest}} update --dry-run  # show what would change
```

It never touches a room or `modelroom.json`.

# Read a modelroom room

A room is one screen. What it delivers is the **docs and the snapshot png**;
`index.html` is only the source the picture is drawn from. Read the picture, not
just the markup.

## Steps

1. Find the room: `rooms/<room>/` (the rooms directory is `rooms` unless
   `modelroom.json` says otherwise).
2. Make the snapshot current. This is idempotent — it writes nothing when the
   png already matches the artifact:

   ```sh
   {{cli}} render <room>
   ```

3. Read `DESIGN.md` at the layer root. It names the design system the rooms draw
   from and, when the project reads it through Model Context Protocol, the MCP
   server that carries it. **Use that server's tools** to look up the components
   and tokens a room uses before you write markup — do not invent a colour or a
   component the design system already defines.
4. When the layer keeps a shared copy of the design system (`vendor/`) or its own
   shared CSS (`design.css`), read those files too — a room links them by relative
   path, and they are what the picture was drawn with. Never edit them from a room's
   work; they are the project's, refreshed by its own script.
5. Read, in order: `BRIEF.md`, `SPEC.md`, `BEHAVIOUR.md`.
6. **Look at `index.png`.** It is the room's screen at the committed width.
   Treat it as the visual source of truth; the html explains how it was drawn.
7. Work from the docs and the picture together. If they disagree, say so — do
   not quietly pick one.

## What the files mean

- `DESIGN.md` — the design system and the tokens/components shared across rooms.
- `design.css`, `vendor/` — the shared copy of those tokens and components; a room links them.
- `BRIEF.md` — why the room exists.
- `SPEC.md` — what the picture cannot show (devices, states, constraints).
- `BEHAVIOUR.md` — what the screen promises, each promise by id (`@checkout-1`).
- `index.png` — the screen, as it was last reviewed.
- `index.html` — the source that picture was rendered from.

## When you change the artifact

The snapshot is the deliverable, so it must match. After editing `index.html`,
run `render <room>` so the committed png is current. This is what the reviewer
reads, and what GitHub diffs on the pull request.

# modelroom の PR を作る

レビュアーはまず画像を読みます。画像がコミットに入り、説明から名前で示されて
いなければ、レビューはマークアップだけになります。

png は**固定名**（`index.png`）でコミットし、毎回その場で上書きします。これは
意図的です。GitHub は**同じパス**の2版を **Files changed → 画像 diff（Swipe /
Onion Skin）** で比較します。タイムスタンプやバージョンを付けて名前を変えな
いでください — 変更のたびに無関係な2ファイルになってしまいます。

## 手順

1. スナップショットを最新にする。冪等で、png が artifact と一致していれば何も
   書きません:

   ```sh
   {{cli}} render <room>
   ```

2. room の変更ファイルを**まとめて**コミットする — docs、`index.html`、
   `index.png`。ステージするのはその room だけにし、無関係な変更を巻き込まない:

   ```sh
   git add rooms/<room>
   ```

3. room から説明の素材を作り、差分のコンテキストは自分で足す:

   ```sh
   {{cli}} pr-body <room>
   ```

   summary、スナップショットの場所、BEHAVIOUR を出力します。何のための変更かを
   短く足してください。

   説明に画像をインラインで出す場合は、レビュアーが描画できる URL（ブランチ上の
   raw ファイル）を渡します:

   ```sh
   {{cli}} pr-body <room> --image-url \
     "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/rooms/<room>/index.png"
   ```

4. PR を作成・更新する:

   ```sh
   gh pr create --title "<room>: <変更内容>" --body-file -
   gh pr edit  --body-file -        # 既存の PR を更新するとき
   ```

## スナップショットをコミットして上書きする理由

- チェックアウトしただけで、何も動かさずに全画面が見える — Playwright も
  サーバも要りません。
- 固定パスであることが、PR の画像 diff を成立させます。
- 通常ならリポジトリを肥大化させるバイナリの積み上がりは、**Squash and Merge**
  でマージすることで抑えられます。main には最終の1枚だけが残り、中間の blob は
  ブランチが消えたあと git が回収します。

画像を base64 にして PR コメントに添えるのはやめてください — GitHub のコメントは
65,536 文字までで、画面はそれをはるかに超えます。

```sh
{{cli}} add <room> --title "Sign in"
```

あとは room を書きます。`BRIEF.md` から始め、最後に次を実行します:

```sh
{{cli}} render <room>
{{cli}} check
```

## room を改名する

動かす前に確認します:

```sh
{{cli}} rename <old> <new> --dry-run
```

dry run はディレクトリの移動と、書き換える参照をすべて表示します。問題なければ
`--dry-run` を外してもう一度実行します。CLI は参照 — `superseded_by` の
frontmatter、`/rooms/<name>` と `/files/<rooms>/<name>` のパス、相対リンク — を
書き換え、旧名をまだ書いている箇所を一覧で出します。

そこから先は手作業です:

1. 一覧の各行を読み、変えるべきか判断します。
2. `title` と H1 はパスではなく文章です。ディレクトリ名と画面の名前は違ってかまい
   ません。画面が本当に改名するときだけ変えます。
3. `{{cli}} check`、`{{cli}} render <room>` の順に実行し、スクリプトが
   見られなかった差分を `git diff` で確認します。

先に `{{cli}}` を止めてください。実行中のサーバは room のチャットセッションを
メモリに持っており、その下で改名すると失われます。サーバが動いている間、コマンドは
実行を拒否します。

## room を削除する

削除は人間の判断です。エージェントは room を退役させます:

```yaml
deprecated: true
superseded_by: <置き換えた room>
```

人間が明確に削除を求めたときだけ、次を実行します:

```sh
{{cli}} remove <room> --dry-run   # 誰がまだ参照しているか
{{cli}} remove <room> --yes
```

`remove` は他の room が参照している間は拒否します（`--force` で続行）。強制削除は
参照を壊したままにするので、必ず直してください。git 以外に元に戻す手段はないので、
削除は単独でコミットしておきます。

## 生成物を更新する

スキルと `AGENTS.md` はインストールされた modelroom から生成されるため、新しい
バージョンで内容が変わります:

```sh
{{cliLatest}} update            # 生成物を更新
{{cliLatest}} update --dry-run  # 変更内容の確認
```

room と `modelroom.json` には一切触れません。

# modelroom の room を読む

room は1画面です。成果物は **docs とスナップショット png** で、`index.html` は
その画像を描くためのソースにすぎません。マークアップだけでなく、画像を読みます。

## 手順

1. room を見つける: `rooms/<room>/`（`modelroom.json` に別の指定がなければ
   rooms ディレクトリは `rooms`）。
2. スナップショットを最新にする。冪等なので、png が artifact と一致していれば
   何も書きません:

   ```sh
   {{cli}} render <room>
   ```

3. レイヤーのルートにある `DESIGN.md` を読みます。rooms がどのデザインシステムから
   描くか、そしてプロジェクトがそれを Model Context Protocol 経由で読む場合は、それを
   運ぶ MCP サーバが書かれています。マークアップを書く前に、**そのサーバのツールを
   使って** room が使うコンポーネントとトークンを調べます。デザインシステムが既に
   定義している色やコンポーネントを作り直してはいけません。
4. レイヤーがデザインシステムの共有コピー（`vendor/`）やレイヤー自身の共有 CSS
   （`design.css`）を持っている場合は、それらも読みます。room は相対パスで読み込んで
   おり、画像はそれで描かれています。room の作業として編集してはいけません。それらは
   プロジェクトのもので、プロジェクトのスクリプトが更新します。
5. `BRIEF.md`、`SPEC.md`、`BEHAVIOUR.md` の順に読む。
6. **`index.png` を見る。** これがコミットされた幅での room の画面です。視覚の
   正は画像とし、html はそれがどう描かれたかの説明として扱います。
7. docs と画像を突き合わせて作業します。食い違っていたら黙って片方を選ばず、
   その旨を伝えます。

## 各ファイルの意味

- `DESIGN.md` — デザインシステムと、room をまたいで共有するトークン・コンポーネント。
- `design.css`、`vendor/` — それらのトークンとコンポーネントの共有コピー。room が読み込む。
- `BRIEF.md` — その room が存在する理由。
- `SPEC.md` — 画像では見えないもの（デバイス、状態、制約）。
- `BEHAVIOUR.md` — 画面が約束するふるまい。約束は id で参照します（`@checkout-1`）。
- `index.png` — 最後にレビューされた画面。
- `index.html` — その画像を描いたソース。

## artifact を変えたとき

スナップショットが成果物なので、必ず一致させます。`index.html` を編集したら
`render <room>` を実行し、コミットする png を最新にしてください。レビュアーが
読むのはその画像で、PR では GitHub がその差分を表示します。

# modelroom

[![CI](https://github.com/modelroom/modelroom/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/modelroom/modelroom/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/modelroom/modelroom/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/modelroom/modelroom)
[![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/modelroom/modelroom/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/modelroom/modelroom)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/modelroom.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/modelroom)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**A full-scale model room for UI — convincing, not yet real.**

modelroom is a workspace for designing screens with coding agents. Each screen is a **room**:
a reason (`BRIEF.md`), an invisible spec (`SPEC.md`), a set of promises (`BEHAVIOUR.md`) and the
artifact (`index.html`) — kept apart, side by side, on one page.

It is agent-agnostic. Bring OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, or any CLI. modelroom bundles no model
and no chat product: it gives your agent a place to work, and gives you a place to look.

![The dashboard: every room with its snapshot, narrowed by facets built from the records](docs/images/dashboard.png)

```bash
npx modelroom init checkout    # asks the language, then a room with its docs
npx modelroom                  # → http://127.0.0.1:4321
```

`init` keeps the design layer in one place — `modelroom/` for what you commit and
`.modelroom/` for local state — and asks which language to use (↑/↓ then Enter; pass
`--lang en` / `--lang ja` to answer it without being asked):

```
your-repo/
├── modelroom/                 # committed
│   ├── modelroom.json
│   ├── AGENTS.md
│   ├── DESIGN.md
│   ├── .agents/skills/        # read-modelroom, create-modelroom-pr, manage-modelroom-rooms
│   └── rooms/checkout/
│       ├── BRIEF.md
│       ├── SPEC.md
│       ├── BEHAVIOUR.md
│       ├── index.html
│       └── index.png
└── .modelroom/                # git-ignored state
```

| Path | Committed? | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `modelroom/modelroom.json` | yes | the config: agent, rooms, language |
| `modelroom/AGENTS.md` | yes | what the agent may write, and in which language |
| `modelroom/DESIGN.md` | yes | the layer's design rules: tokens, components, the design system and its MCP server |
| `modelroom/.agents/skills/` | yes | the agent's three skills: read the picture, put it in the PR, manage rooms |
| `modelroom/rooms/<room>/` | yes | one screen: `BRIEF`, `SPEC`, `BEHAVIOUR`, the artifact, its snapshot `index.png` |
| `.modelroom/state.json` | no | local session ids and settings changed from `/settings` |

`.modelroom/` is disposable: delete it to reset sessions and local settings. The committed
design layer is untouched.

If the repository already has a `package.json`, `init` also adds a `modelroom` script, so
the everyday command is `npm run modelroom` — the way `npm run storybook` works. The package
is installed with your own package manager (detected from the lockfile), so the script runs
the pinned local version; `--skip-install` writes that manager's runner instead
(`"pnpm dlx modelroom"`, `"npx --yes modelroom"`, …) and touches no dependencies, and
`--no-script` leaves `package.json` alone entirely. A `package.json` is never created:
`npx modelroom` stays the default for a project without one.

The command the layer tells your agent to run follows the same manager. `AGENTS.md`, the
skills and the CLI's `next:` line say `pnpm modelroom render <room>` in a pnpm project,
`npm run modelroom` in an npm one, and so on — never a hardcoded `npx`. That is what makes
it work in a project that pins its manager through `devEngines`: npm refuses every command
there, `npx modelroom` included.

## Why "model room"

A model room in real estate is furnished, full scale, and convincing enough to decide in — but it
is not the apartment you will live in. That is the point: decide here, build the real thing after.
The design layer is the model room; implementation is the building.

Because a room is **not** the real thing, the promises that only the real system can keep —
records, timestamps, rounding, permissions — do not live here. The design layer never reads your
application code.

## What you get

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `/` | every room, side by side, with its snapshot — full-text search and filters built from the records. Click a room to preview it without leaving the list |
| `/rooms/<name>` | chat beside one tabbed surface: the artifact, the room's docs, and the session — updating as the agent works |
| `/settings` | which agent to run, and with which model |
| `/files/<path>` | the design layer (`modelroom/`), served read-only and **unmodified** (no injected scripts) |

**The dashboard** is the front page: every room, its snapshot, and the facets the records build.
Click a room and it opens from the right — a preview, not a page.

A room's docs are read-only in the UI — you change them by asking the agent. Changing `index.html`
(from the agent or by hand) reloads the preview with no manual refresh; changes elsewhere in the
room stream in the same way.

Each room also keeps `index.png` — its artifact rendered, committed under a fixed name. That is
the picture a reviewer reads: it shows on the dashboard, and a pull request diffs it under
**Files changed**. Rendering needs Playwright; reading a snapshot does not, which is why it is
committed. See [`docs/05-preview-images.md`](docs/05-preview-images.md).

## The convention in one table

| File | Answers | Shown to |
|---|---|---|
| `BRIEF.md` | why does this room exist? | director, everyone |
| `SPEC.md` | what the artifact cannot show (devices, states, constraints, what it may use) | designer, agent, implementer |
| `BEHAVIOUR.md` | what it promises (operations and results) | tests, implementer |
| `index.html` | what it looks like — the artifact itself | director, owner, implementer |

Two rules do the work: **the artifact owns what is visible** (specs never restate it), and **a
statement lives in one file** (others reference it by id). See [`docs/02-convention.md`](docs/02-convention.md).

Each room's frontmatter is its record. A few keys are reserved (`title`, `summary`,
`key_points`, `tags`, `status`, `version`, `deprecated`, `superseded_by`, `device`);
**everything else becomes a facet on the dashboard automatically** — a string turns into
a select, a list into checkboxes, built from the values that actually exist. Search covers
the docs, not just the titles. `device` is also how a room picks the screen its snapshot
is rendered at; `docs/03-cli.md` has the details.

```yaml
---
title: Sign in
status: draft
version: 1
summary: A boring front door — signed in, or told plainly why not.
tags: [auth, form]
---
```

An agent adds; it does not delete. Retiring a room is `deprecated: true` plus
`superseded_by: <room>`, so the record stays and git can bring it back. `modelroom check`
verifies the convention without writing anything. `adopted` is a human decision — an agent
must never set it.

Rooms are made, renamed and removed with the CLI — `npx modelroom add`, `rename`, `remove`
— so the unique directory name and the references to it move together. `modelroom update`
refreshes the generated skills and `AGENTS.md` when you upgrade; `DESIGN.md` is yours and is
left alone. `serve`, the dashboard and `doctor` say when a newer modelroom exists, with the
command that fits this project — and modelroom never installs it for you.

What every room shares is shared **once**. `DESIGN.md` records the decisions, `design.css`
holds the layer's own tokens and components, and a vendored design system lives under
`vendor/`; a room links both by relative path, so the artifact still renders offline. No CDN,
no per-room copy of the framework, no build step.

## Agents

```jsonc
// modelroom/modelroom.json
{
  "root": ".",
  "rooms": "rooms",
  "state": "../.modelroom",
  "lang": "ja",                                // optional; init writes it when you answer
  "agent": {
    "adapter": "opencode",                       // or "command" for any CLI
    "command": "opencode",
    "agent": "build",
    "model": "openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash",
    "standalone": true
  }
}
```

`adapter: "command"` runs anything: `{ "command": "claude", "args": ["-p", "{prompt}"] }`.
Full detail, including how to scope an agent so it can only write room files, is in
[`docs/04-agents.md`](docs/04-agents.md).

## From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/modelroom/modelroom && cd modelroom
npm install                 # dev only: builds the UI (Mantine + React bundled) + playwright (optional)
npm test                    # smoke checks
npm run modelroom           # serves templates/en/example/rooms
npm run build:css           # after changing web/*.html or client/modelroom.css
npm run build:client        # after changing client/**
```

`npm install` builds the stylesheet and the JS bundle in `web/` (via `prepare`), and the
published package ships them already built, so users never run a build step; neither file is
committed. The tool's UI is React + [Mantine](https://mantine.dev); the artifacts (in
`templates/`) are deliberately plain HTML and CSS — no CDN, no web fonts, no build step —
because they are handed to implementation and must render with no network. A project that
adopts a design system can keep one copy for the whole layer and link it from its rooms: see
[`docs/02-convention.md`](docs/02-convention.md).

Snapshots need Playwright to be rendered; reviewing them needs nothing:

```bash
npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium
modelroom render --all          # bring every room's index.png up to date
modelroom render --all --check   # CI: is a snapshot out of date?
```

## Development

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev        # serve, watching the source
npm run verify     # lint, types, format, tests, build — the same gates as CI
```

Source is TypeScript (erasable syntax only) and runs directly on Node 22.18+. `npm run build`
emits `dist/` with declarations; that is what npm publishes. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the rules.

## What it is not

- Not an app builder (v0, Lovable, bolt.new). Those put chat first; this puts the room first.
- Not a fork of anything. It is a convention plus a small local server.
- Not a replacement for your agent. It drives the one you already use.
- Not an installer. It tells you when a newer modelroom exists and prints the command that
  fits your project; it never writes your `package.json` or lockfile.

# Concept

modelroom is the **design layer** for software built with coding agents. It is a convention
plus a small local server; it does not bundle a model or a chat product.

## The model room

A model room in real estate is furnished, full scale, and convincing enough to decide in —
but it is not the apartment you will live in. The design layer works the same way:

- it is **not the real thing** (no database, no server clock, no permissions);
- it is **convincing enough** that a decision can be made in it;
- each room is **shown to someone** before the real build starts.

Everything below follows from that one property: because a room is not the real thing, the
promises that only the real thing can keep live somewhere else.

## Layers and who each file is shown to

Files are named by **what they are**, and each one has one audience. The audience decides
the wording.

| File | Answers | Written by | Shown to | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BRIEF.md` | Why does this exist? What matters most? | director | director, everyone | humans |
| `SPEC.md` | What is on the screen that you cannot see? (devices, states, constraints, references) | designer | designer, agent, implementer | humans |
| `BEHAVIOUR.md` | What does it do? (operations and results) | designer | tests, implementer | system tests |
| `index.html`, `index.png` | What it looks like | agent | director, owner, implementer | screenshots + humans |
| `principles.md`, `components.md`, `design-tokens/` | The shared interior rules | designer | everyone | humans + tokens |

Two rules keep this from drifting:

1. **The artifact owns what is visible.** `SPEC.md` never lists what can be seen in
   `index.html`; if a statement can be shown in a screenshot, it belongs to the artifact.
2. **No statement lives in two files.** If a rule must reach another file, reference it
   (one line, by id) instead of copying it.

## One-way dependency

```
app  ──reads──▶  design        (artifacts, tokens)
design ──✗──▶    app           (the design layer never reads the application)
```

The design layer must not read the application. A model room has no plumbing, so promises
that depend on the real system (records, rounding, closing, permissions) are owned by the
application layer and are never copied here. What the design layer needs to know is handed
to it — in a brief, in an issue, or in conversation.

This is enforceable, not aspirational: an agent working in the design directory can be
denied access outside it.

## What "behaviour" means here

`BEHAVIOUR.md` holds promises that the room itself can keep — operations and results that a
system test can observe. Promises that need the real system (for example, that a record
carries the server's timestamp) belong to the application layer, not to this file.

## Why this shape

Agents make writing cheap; they do not make **agreement** cheap. A workspace that keeps the
reason (`BRIEF`), the invisible spec (`SPEC`), the promise (`BEHAVIOUR`) and the result (the
artifact) in separate, single-purpose files lets several agents — and several people — work
on the same screen without overwriting one another's meaning.

# The convention A room is one screen. Everything in a room is a file with one job, and every file has one audience. That is the whole idea; the rest follows. ## Files ``` modelroom/ ├── AGENTS.md how to work in this layer → agent ├── DESIGN.md the layer's design rules → designer, agent ├── modelroom.json ├── .agents/skills/ the agent's three skills ├── vendor// the design system, copied once, pinned → every room ├── design.css the layer's shared tokens and components → every room └── rooms// ├── BRIEF.md why this room exists → director, everyone ├── SPEC.md what the artifact cannot show → designer, agent, implementer ├── BEHAVIOUR.md what it promises → tests, implementer ├── index.html the artifact (the screen) → director, owner, implementer └── index.png the screen, as reviewed → reviewer, agent ``` Local state lives in `.modelroom/` next to `modelroom/`, and is never committed. `DESIGN.md` holds what every room shares — the tokens, the components, the accessibility floor — and names the design system they come from (and the MCP server that carries it, when there is one). A room takes from it and names what it took in its `SPEC.md`. It is the project's file: `init` seeds it once, `update` never touches it. Two files above are shared and never a room's: `vendor//` is the design system itself, copied once and pinned, and `design.css` is the layer's own CSS. A room links both; see *The design system, shared once* below. `init` starts a layer with neither — the first time two rooms need the same thing, they appear. The artifact is the visible spec. `SPEC.md` is the invisible one. They must not overlap. `index.png` is the artifact **rendered** — the same screen as a picture, committed next to it under a fixed name. It is what a reviewer reads and what a pull request diffs; the html is the source it was drawn from. See `05-preview-images.md` for why it is committed and how it is kept current. ## Rules 1. **The artifact owns what is visible.** If a statement can be shown in a screenshot, it belongs to `index.html`, not to `SPEC.md`. The snapshot is that screenshot: when the artifact changes, regenerate it (`modelroom render`) so the room the reviewer reads is the room that was drawn. 2. **A statement lives in one file.** To reach another file, reference it by id (`@sign-in-1`) instead of copying it. 3. **The design layer never reads the application.** Rooms hold promises the room itself can keep. Anything that needs the real system — records, timestamps, rounding, permissions — belongs to the application and is handed over, not fetched. 4. **Implementation reads the design layer, never the other way round.** This is enforceable rather than aspirational: an agent working in the design layer can be denied access outside it (for example, OpenCode `permissions` with `external_directory: deny` and write rules limited to `rooms/*`). ## The artifact - **Self-contained means no network and no build step.** It is going to be handed to implementation, so it has to stand on its own: no CDN, no web fonts, nothing to install, nothing to compile. Open `index.html` from disk and the screen is there. It does *not* mean one file — a room may link what the layer shares (below). - One file per state (`index-error.html` and so on). Steps in a flow are separate rooms. - Anything shared (a component, a token) is decided in the layer's `DESIGN.md` and named in `SPEC.md`; it is written once for the layer, not reinvented per room. ## The design system, shared once A project that draws from a real design system — Bootstrap, a house system, a vendor kit — keeps **one** copy for the whole layer and lets the rooms link it. Copying the framework into every room is the duplication `DESIGN.md` exists to prevent; hand-writing its components in each room is the same duplication, one layer out. ``` modelroom/ ├── DESIGN.md names the system, its MCP, and the two files below ├── vendor// the system's files, copied from the pinned package — committed │ └── MANIFEST.json the version, and a sha256 per file ├── design.css the layer's own shared CSS: its tokens, its components — committed └── rooms//index.html ``` - **One copy, at the layer root, outside `rooms/`.** Never per room, never a CDN. - **A room links it, relative to itself**, so the same path resolves whether the artifact is opened from disk (`file://`, what `render` does) or served at `/files/rooms//index.html`: ```html ``` - **It is committed**, so the artifact renders with no network and travels with the layer when the layer is handed over. - **The version is pinned and recorded.** The manifest next to the copy carries the version and a hash per file, and a script the project owns refreshes it from the package manager's cache; bumping the framework is one reviewable commit, not a search through rooms. - **A room keeps what is its own.** Only what two rooms would otherwise repeat moves to `design.css`; a room's own styles stay in the room. - **`SPEC.md` says what the room took and at which version.** Implementation installs the same version through its own dependency manager — the vendored copy is how the design layer draws the screen, not the production dependency. Saying so is what tells the implementer what to expect on the other side. ## Frontmatter is the record The body is the content. The frontmatter is the record the dashboard reads: the title, the one-line summary, the tags, the state. Nothing else stores it, so nothing has to be kept in sync. ```yaml --- title: Sign in status: draft version: 1 summary: A boring front door — the person is signed in, or told plainly why not. tags: [auth, form] --- ``` Reserved keys — shape only, never a fixed vocabulary: | Key | Shape | Shown as | |---|---|---| | `title` | string | the card's heading | | `summary` | string | one line under the heading | | `key_points` | string[] | up to three bullets | | `tags` | string[] | chips, and a checkbox facet | | `status` | string | a badge, and a facet | | `version` | number or string | a `v3` badge | | `updated_at` | date string, or epoch ms | sort order (falls back to file mtime) | | `deprecated` | boolean | hidden unless archived is on | | `superseded_by` | string | a pointer to the room that replaced this one | | `device` | string | the device the snapshot renders at (`sp`, `tablet`, `pc`, or a name from `modelroom.json`) | | `next` | string | the main transition: the next room in the flow | | `app` | string | which application a room belongs to; the flow view groups by it | `next` and `app` are how a set of rooms becomes a flow. `app` is free text — `user`, `admin`, `user-legacy` — and, like every other key, it becomes a facet, so the dashboard's app tabs are just the values that exist. `next` names one room: the main edge the wireframe draws. It should stay inside its own `app`; a `next` that crosses apps is a `modelroom check` warning, because a transition that changes app is a different flow. ```yaml --- title: Sign in app: user next: top --- ``` The flow view draws these as a graph — one tab per `app`, arrows for `next` — and the room cards can be walked in the preview itself: a link inside `index.html` opens the next room's screen. Write it **relative to the room**, so it resolves whether the artifact is opened from disk or served: ```html Sign in ``` An absolute `/rooms/top/index.html` does not work: `/rooms/` is the tool's own address for a room, not a path to a file, and it breaks the disk case too. `device` is the one reserved key with a fixed vocabulary: it must name a device the project knows, because the renderer needs its width and height. `modelroom check` reports a name that does not resolve. **Everything else is a facet.** Add `category: kiosk`, `platform: tablet`, or anything that helps you narrow the list; a string becomes a radio group or a select (built from the values that exist, with counts), a list becomes checkboxes. The dashboard never validates values — it shows what is there. `adopted` (or `accepted`, `approved`) is a human decision. An agent must never set it. ## What an agent may do An agent adds. It does not delete. - new room, new key, new tag, new doc → fine - merge two spellings → add an alias, leave both values in place - retire a room → `deprecated: true` and `superseded_by: ` - remove a file or a key → a human does it A room is created, renamed and removed through the CLI (`modelroom add`, `rename`, `remove`), because the directory name is the room and the references to it have to move with it. `rename` rewrites the references it can see and lists the prose it leaves; a removal takes `--yes` and is refused while another room points at the room. That is what makes "the agent keeps the record tidy" safe: every move is additive and reversible in git. ## The check ``` modelroom check ``` It reads the frontmatter — head of the file only — and reports what would stop the dashboard from deriving the record: malformed or nested frontmatter, a reserved key with the wrong shape, two spellings of the same value, a `title` that disagrees with the H1, a `superseded_by` that points nowhere. Errors are fixable by an agent; warnings are for a human. It never writes. ## Naming - Files are named for **what they are**, not for who writes them and not for the tool: `BRIEF`, `SPEC`, `BEHAVIOUR`, `DESIGN`, `principles`, `components`, `tokens`. - Avoid words that shift meaning with the reader (`context`, `system`, `ui`, `ux`) and words that name a medium (`screen`, `page`) when the thing is not a medium. - **Scope is expressed by the directory, not by the filename.** One `BRIEF.md` per level — product, flow, room — read top-down, written only at your own level. - Prefer one word that survives translation (see the list above) over a compound.

# CLI

```
modelroom [serve] [--port 4321] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--open] [--lang en|ja]
modelroom init [<room>] [--dir rooms] [--lang en|ja] [--force] [--skip-install] [--no-script]
modelroom add <room> [--title "Sign in"]
modelroom rename <old> <new> [--dry-run] [--force]
modelroom remove <room> [--yes] [--dry-run] [--force]
modelroom update [--dry-run]
modelroom check [--json] [--strict]
modelroom doctor
modelroom render [<room>] [--all] [--check] [--force] [--device <name>]
modelroom pr-body <room> [--image-url <url>]
modelroom --version | --help
```

`modelroom` with no command is `serve`. `serve` needs Node 20+ and nothing else. `init`
copies templates and asks which language to use. `add`, `rename` and `remove` keep the rooms
unique and their references in step. `update` refreshes the files modelroom generated.
`check` reads the frontmatter of every room and reports convention problems.

The tool UI does the same three room operations with this same code: the dashboard's **Add
room** button, and the pencil and ⋯ menu in a room's header. A room made in the browser is
byte-identical to one made with the command.
`doctor` checks the setup and exits non-zero when something is broken (optionally missing things
do not count). `render` keeps each room's snapshot png current; `pr-body` prints what a pull
request description should carry.

## serve

Starts the workspace on `127.0.0.1:4321` by default. `modelroom` alone does the same.

- `/` — every room, side by side
- `/rooms/<name>` — chat, the room's docs, the artifact
- `/settings` — which agent to run
- `/files/<path>` — your repository, served read-only and **unmodified** (no injection)

`--open` tries to open a browser; on a headless machine it is ignored.

When there is a newer modelroom, `serve` says so once — after the banner, when the answer
lands — and the dashboard and `/settings` show the same notice with the command that fits
this project. It is a notice, never an install; see **Knowing a newer one exists** under
`update`.

## init

Creates the design layer in `modelroom/` and keeps local state outside it:

```
your-repo/
├── modelroom/                 # committed
│   ├── modelroom.json
│   ├── AGENTS.md
│   ├── DESIGN.md
│   ├── .agents/skills/         # read-modelroom, create-modelroom-pr, manage-modelroom-rooms
│   └── rooms/<room>/{BRIEF,SPEC,BEHAVIOUR}.md + index.html + index.png
└── .modelroom/                # git-ignored state
```

`init` writes the room templates and the three skills, and — if missing —
`modelroom/modelroom.json`, `modelroom/AGENTS.md`, `modelroom/DESIGN.md` and a
`/.modelroom/` line in the project's `.gitignore`.
An existing project keeps its config; running `init` again only adds what is
missing (`--force` overwrites).

The skills go to `.agents/skills/`, the portable location: OpenCode and Claude Code
both read it (OpenCode also reads its own `.opencode/skills/`).

```
modelroom init checkout            # asks which language, then modelroom/rooms/checkout/
modelroom init checkout --dir screens
modelroom init checkout --lang ja  # answer the language question without being asked
modelroom init checkout --force    # overwrite existing files
```

### The `modelroom` script

If the project has a `package.json`, `init` also makes `npm run modelroom` work, the
way `npm run storybook` does — one script, and the package installed so the script
runs the pinned local version:

```jsonc
{
  "scripts": { "modelroom": "modelroom" },
  "devDependencies": { "modelroom": "^0.1.0" }
}
```

- The script is added **only when the key is missing**, and only to a `package.json`
  that already exists — `init` never creates one. A project with no package manager
  keeps `npx modelroom` as its default; this is a convenience for projects that
  already live in npm scripts.
- The dependency is installed with the project's own package manager, detected from
  the lockfile (`bun.lock*`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, otherwise npm). Writing a
  dependency entry by hand would leave the lockfile behind and break `npm ci`, so the
  manager is the only thing that ever touches it.
- `--skip-install` leaves dependencies alone and writes that manager's runner instead
  of the local bin — `"modelroom": "npx --yes modelroom"` for npm, `pnpm dlx modelroom`,
  `yarn dlx modelroom`, `bunx modelroom` — so no install is needed.
- If the install fails (offline, no manager on `PATH`), `init` says so, keeps the
  runner script and continues — the script works either way, and running the printed
  command later upgrades it to the local version.
- The layer modelroom generates follows the same manager: `AGENTS.md`, the three
  skills and the CLI's `next:` line name the command that actually runs here — `npm
  run modelroom`, `pnpm modelroom`, `yarn modelroom`, `bun run modelroom` — not a
  hardcoded `npx`. That matters for a project that pins its manager through
  `devEngines`: npm then refuses **every** command, `npx modelroom` included, so a
  `npx` in the agent's instructions is a command that cannot run. Where no script was
  added, the manager's remote runner stands in (`pnpm dlx modelroom`, `bunx modelroom`,
  otherwise `npx modelroom`).
- `--force` replaces an existing `modelroom` script; `--no-script` keeps `init` out of
  the `package.json` entirely.
- A project whose `package.json` cannot be read as JSON is left untouched, with a note.

### Language

`init` asks which language to use when you run it at a terminal — ↑/↓ to choose, Enter to
confirm, starting on the one it detected. The question is shown in both languages,
because it is asked *because* the detection may be wrong. Escape answers nothing and
leaves the language automatic; Ctrl+C stops `init` with nothing written.

An answer, like `--lang en|ja`, is written to the project's config as `lang` — the
`modelroom/modelroom.json` of the current layout, or the root `modelroom.json` of a
project that has one — and from then on the CLI, the web UI and new rooms all speak it.
A config that already names a language is not asked about again.

When nobody is there to answer — no terminal, or `CI=1` — the language is resolved
without asking, in this order:

1. `lang` in the config, when it is present
2. `MODELROOM_LANG`
3. `LC_ALL` / `LC_MESSAGES` / `LANG`
4. the OS locale
5. English

Detection is a guess, and a poor one on macOS: the OS language is not visible to a Node
process there, only the shell's `LANG`, so a Mac set to Japanese whose shell exports
`LANG=en_US.UTF-8` detects English. That is why a terminal is asked rather than guessed
at. `--lang` answers the question without asking, which is what a script or CI wants.

Existing room documents are never rewritten; the language affects new rooms only. To
translate a project that already has rooms, pin the language and ask the agent to translate
the existing `BRIEF.md` / `SPEC.md` / `BEHAVIOUR.md` files — the frontmatter keys and
promise ids stay as they are.

## add

Adds one room to an existing project — the directory plus every doc the config names and
the artifact. It is additive: an existing directory is never overwritten. `add` is the
name; `new` is a hidden alias.

```
modelroom add checkout
modelroom add checkout --title "Checkout"
```

The name is the room's record, so it must be unique and it must be a lowercase slug
(`a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `-`, `_`). A name that differs only by case from an existing room is
refused, because a case-insensitive disk cannot hold both. `--title` sets the human title
on `BRIEF.md` (frontmatter and H1) while the directory keeps the slug.

```
$ modelroom add sign-in
created room sign-in:
  modelroom/rooms/sign-in/BRIEF.md
  ...
next: npm run modelroom (or open http://127.0.0.1:4321/rooms/sign-in)
```

The `next:` line names the project's own command — `npm run modelroom` when `init`
added the script, `pnpm modelroom`, `yarn modelroom`, `bun run modelroom` in a pnpm,
yarn or bun project, and the manager's remote runner when there is no script.

## rename

Moves the directory and every reference to it. Run it with `--dry-run` first: it prints the
move and what it would rewrite without writing.

```
modelroom rename sign-in sign-in-v2 --dry-run
modelroom rename sign-in sign-in-v2
```

What is a *reference* is rewritten: the `superseded_by` frontmatter, `/rooms/<name>`,
`/files/<rooms>/<name>`, and relative links (`../<name>/…`) in every room's docs and html.
What is *prose* is not — a `title`, an H1, a sentence — because the directory name and the
name on the screen are allowed to differ. Those places are listed so a person (or the
agent) can decide:

```
renamed sign-in → sign-in-v2
rewrite  modelroom/rooms/checkout/SPEC.md  (2 reference(s))
    modelroom/rooms/checkout/SPEC.md:4  superseded_by: sign-in — replaced by
```

The room's chat session moves with it. Because a running `serve` holds that session in
memory, `rename` refuses while a server is up; stop it first, or pass `--force`.

## remove

Deleting a room is a human decision, so it takes `--yes`. An agent retires a room instead
with `deprecated: true` and `superseded_by: <room>`. A room another room points at is
refused unless `--force`, which leaves those references broken.

```
modelroom remove sign-in --dry-run    # who still points at it? (writes nothing)
modelroom remove sign-in --yes
```

`--dry-run` reports before it refuses, so it always shows the referencing rooms. There is no
undo beyond git: commit the removal on its own so it can be reverted.

## update

Refreshes the files modelroom generated — the skills in `.agents/skills/` and `AGENTS.md`
— from the installed version. Those change with the version, so this is how an existing
project picks them up. `@latest` fetches the new version first, so use the manager's
remote runner when the project pins one (`pnpm dlx modelroom@latest`, `yarn dlx`,
`bunx`):

```
npx modelroom@latest update
npx modelroom@latest update --dry-run
```

It never touches a room, `DESIGN.md` or `modelroom.json`: those are the project's, not
modelroom's. A new install gets the same generated files from `init`.

`update` acts on the version that is installed, so on its own it cannot upgrade anything.
It is the second half of the command below.

### Knowing a newer one exists

`serve` and `doctor` say so, and so do the dashboard and `/settings`:

```
  update   modelroom 0.6.0 is available — npm install --save-dev modelroom@latest && npm run modelroom update
```

The command is the project's own — its package manager, its script, or the manager's remote
runner where `init` added no script — so it is the one that works in this repository: install
the newer modelroom, then let that copy refresh the files it generated.

- The check is a single GET to `registry.npmjs.org`, at most once a day, with a two-second
  timeout. The answer is cached in `.modelroom/state.json` (git-ignore it), and a failure is
  silent: offline, `serve` starts and says nothing about versions.
- **Nothing is installed for you.** modelroom never writes the consumer's `package.json` or
  lockfile — a dependency entry written by hand would leave the lockfile behind and break
  `npm ci` — so the notice stops at the command. Run it where you can read what the package
  manager says, and restart `serve` afterwards: the process keeps running the version it
  started with.
- `MODELROOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` turns the check off, and it is the only thing in modelroom
  that talks to the network. A checkout ahead of the registry — a branch, a release that is
  not published yet — is not an "update", and stays quiet.
- `doctor` never fails on it: a newer modelroom is not a problem, it is a decision.

## check

```
modelroom check              # errors and warnings
modelroom check --json       # machine-readable
modelroom check --strict     # warnings fail too
```

It only reads the head of each doc (frontmatter lives there) and never writes:

```
FAIL  sign-in/BRIEF.md  reserved-type  tags must be array, got string
warn  checkout/BRIEF.md  h1-title       H1 "Checkout" differs from title "check out"
warn  sign-in/BRIEF.md   variant        status: draft / Draft — same value, different spelling

2 room(s), 1 error(s), 2 warning(s)
```

Exit code is 1 on errors (or on warnings with `--strict`).

## render

`render` produces the snapshot png next to a room's artifact. It is idempotent: a room
is rendered only when its artifact — or a doc that names its device — moved after the last
render, and a render whose bytes do not change writes nothing, so the committed file moves
only when the picture does. What the last render drew from is kept in local state
(`.modelroom/state.json`), not in the png's timestamp: `docs/05-preview-images.md` says why.

```
modelroom render checkout          # one room, only if stale
modelroom render --all             # every room, the stale ones only
modelroom render checkout --force  # render even when it looks current
modelroom render checkout --device pc
```

By default each room renders at the device it names in its frontmatter (`device:`),
falling back to `thumbnail.device`. `--device` overrides both for that run — useful for
looking at one room on another screen, but not what you commit: `--check` and `serve`
use the room's own device, so a one-off override would show up as a stale snapshot.

`serve` runs the same pass in the background: on start, when an artifact changes, and
whenever the dashboard asks for the room list. You do not have to call `render` to make
the tool work; you call it to be sure a commit carries the current picture.

`--check` renders to a temporary file and compares instead of writing:

```
modelroom render --all --check
ok      checkout  (snapshot matches, pc)
stale   sign-in   (snapshot no longer matches index.html, sp)

1 snapshot(s) out of date
```

Exit code is 1 when a snapshot is missing or out of date — the gate for CI, and the way
to prove that a change meant to be invisible (an accessibility fix, a refactor) left the
pixels alone.

Rendering needs Playwright:

```
npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium
```

Without it, `render` reports what is missing and the room keeps whatever snapshot is
already committed — which is exactly the point of committing it.

## pr-body

Prints, as markdown, what a pull request description should carry: the room's title and
summary, where its snapshot is, and its `BEHAVIOUR.md`.

```
modelroom pr-body checkout --image-url \
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/rooms/checkout/index.png"
```

Without `--image-url` it points the reviewer at the file instead of embedding it — the
primary way to read the picture is the pull request's **Files changed** image diff. The
command does not touch git or `gh`; those belong to the agent, which knows the branch and
the repository.

```jsonc
  "lang": "ja",                                 // optional; omitted = auto. "en" | "ja"
  "artifact": "index.html",                     // the file that is the screen
```

`root` is what `/files/...` and the agent's working directory see. With a new

Anything you change from `/settings` is kept locally in `.modelroom/state.json`
