## Snapshots

Each room keeps a png next to its artifact, rendered at one device and one scale. It is a
deliverable, not a cache: it is committed with the room, a reviewer reads it, and a pull
request diffs it.

The device is resolved per room: an explicit `--device`, then the room's frontmatter
`device:`, then `thumbnail.device`. Three devices are built in — `sp` (390×844),
`tablet` (1024×768) and `pc` (1280×800) — and `devices` in `modelroom.json` adds or
redefines them by name:

```jsonc
"devices": {
  "kiosk": { "width": 1024, "height": 768, "rotated": false },
  "admin": { "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
}
```

A room names its surface in its frontmatter:

```yaml
---
title: Shift board
device: kiosk
---
```

A project whose rooms are all one surface sets `thumbnail.device` once and never thinks
about it. `thumbnail.device` and `thumbnail.scale` are committed configuration; changing
the default re-renders the rooms that do not name their own device, so keep it steady.

Rendering needs Playwright:

```
npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium
```

Without it, nothing breaks: a room keeps whatever snapshot is already committed, and
`render` (or the **make png** button) reports what is missing. Committing the png is what
lets someone review a room without installing anything.

The full reasoning — why the png is committed, why the name never changes, and why the
merge is a squash — is in `05-preview-images.md`.

# Agents

modelroom does not bundle a model and does not own a chat product. It runs the agent you
configure, one session per room, and shows you what changed.

## Built-in adapters

| Adapter | What it runs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode` | [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) CLI | sessions, model and agent selection |
| `command` | any CLI | you provide `agent.args`; `{prompt}` and `{session}` are substituted |

### opencode

```jsonc
{
  "agent": {
    "adapter": "opencode",
    "command": "opencode",
    "agent": "build",           // an agent defined in .opencode/agents/
    "model": "openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash",
    "standalone": true
  }
}
```

modelroom runs a private OpenCode server of its own and drives the turn through its API:

```
opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port <free>   # one per modelroom process
```

It creates the room's session (`POST /api/session`), sends the prompt
(`POST /api/session/<id>/prompt`), and follows the turn until the session goes idle. That is
the same private server `--standalone` starts, only kept alive across turns — and it is the
point of the whole thing: a one-shot `opencode run` has nobody to answer the agent's question,
so it cancels the question and the tool errors instead.

Two things are worth knowing, both learned the hard way:

- **Set `model`.** Many agents resolve to a free tier by default, and the CLI then refuses to
  run outside its own app (`OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`).
- **The private server inherits this process's environment**, which is what makes provider keys
  visible to it. `standalone` no longer changes how opencode is run — modelroom always owns its
  own server — and stays in the config for compatibility.

### What the chat shows

modelroom runs the agent, but it does not read the *turn* out of the CLI's prose. It reads the
session the server is writing: the text, the reasoning, one entry per tool call, and the patch an
edit wrote. So a tool call is a row you can open, an edit shows its diff, and reasoning folds
away. The turn ends when the session goes idle, not when a process exits.

If the session cannot be reached, or the adapter has no such place to look, the chat is exactly
what the process printed. That is the `command` adapter, and it is why `structured` exists.

### Questions

An agent that needs a decision asks a question and blocks on it. modelroom answers the
permission requests the way `opencode run --auto` would — a request that *asks* is approved, a
configured `deny` is respected — and it does **not** answer questions on the person's behalf. It
shows the question above the composer, with the agent's options and a free-form field; the answer
goes back to the same turn, and the agent carries on from where it stopped.

The question is opencode's `form`; modelroom projects it onto the driver-agnostic `Ask`
(`api/chat.ts`) so the chat never learns opencode's shape. A second driver (Claude Code, say)
would produce the same `Ask` and reuse the same card.

The agent runs with its working directory set to `cfg.rootDir` — for a new
install, `modelroom/`. That is where it reads `AGENTS.md`, and it is the whole
tree modelroom will serve under `/files/...`.

Agents that need to *write* only the room's files should be scoped on their side, for example
with OpenCode `permissions`:

```yaml
# modelroom/.opencode/agents/design.md
permissions:
  - { action: "*", resource: "*", effect: deny }
  - { action: read, resource: "rooms/*", effect: allow }
  - { action: edit, resource: "rooms/*", effect: allow }
  - { action: glob, resource: "*", effect: allow }
  - { action: grep, resource: "*", effect: allow }
  - { action: external_directory, resource: "*", effect: deny }
```

### command

For anything else — Claude Code, Codex, a local model, a shell script:

```jsonc
{
  "agent": { "adapter": "command", "command": "claude", "args": ["-p", "{prompt}"] }
}
```

`{session}` is substituted with the room's session id. Sessions are stored per room in
`.modelroom/state.json` at the project root; **new session** in the room UI starts a fresh one.

The generated `AGENTS.md` tells the agent which language to write the room's prose in, and
that frontmatter keys and promise ids stay in English. Change `lang` in `modelroom.json`
to change that language for new rooms and for the UI; existing documents are not rewritten.

## The snapshot and the pull request

A room's reviewable output is the docs and the snapshot `index.png`, not the markup. An
agent that only reads `index.html` is reading half the room, so the layer ships three skills
(`init` writes them to `modelroom/.agents/skills/`):

| Skill | When | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `read-modelroom` | before changing or implementing a room | `render` (idempotent), then read the docs **and the picture** |
| `create-modelroom-pr` | when a change is ready to review | `render`, commit the room's files together, open a PR with the image, the context and the BEHAVIOUR |
| `manage-modelroom-rooms` | a room is added, renamed or removed | use the CLI so the unique name and its references move together |

The first two lean on two commands:

```
modelroom render <room>            # bring the snapshot up to date
modelroom render <room> --check    # prove the pixels did not move (CI gate)
modelroom pr-body <room>           # the description's material, as markdown
```

Rooms are added, renamed and removed through the CLI, which is what keeps the directory name
unique and the references to it in step: `modelroom add`, `rename` and `remove`. The script
rewrites what is a reference (`superseded_by`, `/rooms/<name>`, relative links) and lists the
prose it leaves alone; the skill carries the reasoning and the approval a removal needs.
When the layer is upgraded, `modelroom update` refreshes the skills and `AGENTS.md` — the
files modelroom generated — and never `DESIGN.md`, a room or `modelroom.json`. Upgrading is
a person's decision: when `serve`, the dashboard or `doctor` says a newer modelroom exists,
name the command and leave it there — modelroom does not install anything, and neither
should an agent.

Skills are plain `SKILL.md` files. They are written to `.agents/skills/`, which OpenCode
and Claude Code both read; OpenCode also reads its own `.opencode/skills/`. To use the
shipped skills with an agent that reads neither, copy or symlink the three directories.

**modelroom never touches git or `gh`.** It renders and prints; the agent owns the branch,
the commit and the pull request. That is the same line the rest of the design layer holds:
the tool stays inside `rooms/` and hands the rest over.

Merge the pull request with **Squash and Merge**. The snapshot is a binary under a fixed
name, so the branch holds one per revision; squashing leaves main with a single current
image and lets git collect the rest. `05-preview-images.md` has the reasoning.

## The design system, and MCP

A room is drawn from the project's design system, and an agent often reads that design
system through its **MCP server** — component and token lookups instead of guessing. The
layer keeps the two halves apart:

- `DESIGN.md` names the design system, where its truth lives, and the MCP server that
  carries it. It is the project's file; `update` never touches it.
- When the rooms are drawn *with* that system, the layer keeps one copy of it — `vendor/` for
  third-party files and the layer's own shared CSS beside it — and a room links the copy by
  relative path, so it renders offline and travels with the layer. `DESIGN.md` names the copy
  and the version it was taken from; `docs/02-convention.md` ("The design system, shared once")
  has the rules. A room never installs a framework of its own.
- The server itself is *configured* in `opencode.json`. modelroom runs `opencode serve`
  with its working directory set to the layer (`modelroom/`), so OpenCode reads
  `modelroom/opencode.json`, plus any `opencode.json` above it up to the repository root.
  Add the server under `mcp`:

  ```json
  {
    "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
    "mcp": {
      "design-system": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://example.com/mcp" }
    }
  }
  ```

  OpenCode V2 nests these under `mcp.servers` instead. Keep secrets in the environment —
  OpenCode substitutes `{env:NAME}` — and out of the committed file.

  The room's MCP panel reads its list from that same server, the one the turn runs on —
  not from the shared `opencode` service, whose servers belong to another directory — so
  what the panel lists is what the agent can actually call.

There is no portable MCP file across agents: `.mcp.json` is Claude Code's,
`.cursor/mcp.json` is Cursor's, `.vscode/mcp.json` is VS Code's, and OpenCode reads none
of them. If the layer is driven by more than one agent, each gets its own file; OpenCode's
is `opencode.json`. The shipped `read-modelroom` skill carries the *how*: read `DESIGN.md`,
use the design system's MCP tools before writing markup, and read the vendored copy the room
links when there is one.

## Writing an adapter

An adapter is one object:

```js
export const mine = {
  name: 'mine',
  structured: false, // true only if the turn can be read while it still runs
  newSessionId: () => `ses_${Date.now().toString(36)}${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`,
  run({ cfg, cwd, prompt, sessionId, onChunk, onExit }) {
    // spawn your CLI; stream output with onChunk('stdout'|'stderr', text)
    // call onExit(code, errorMessage?) once it finishes
  },
};
```

Add it to `server/agents/index.ts`. Three rules keep adapters honest:

1. **Close stdin** (`stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']`). A CLI that reads stdin will hang
   forever if the pipe stays open.
2. **Do not parse the output into meaning.** modelroom shows the agent's words as they are.
   Interpretation belongs to the person reading the room.
3. **`structured: true` is a claim that the turn can be read while the run is in progress** —
   that the agent keeps it somewhere modelroom can ask for it. The reading lives in
   `server/opencode.ts` (`sessionParts`). If the claim is wrong, the agent's *prose* lands in the
   chat and nothing else breaks.

`run` is optional: an adapter without one is driven by modelroom itself rather than by a spawned
process. The `opencode` adapter is that case — modelroom owns an `opencode serve` and follows the
turn through its API (`server/opencode-turn.ts`), which is what lets a question stay open long
enough for the person to answer it.

# Preview images

A room is reviewed as a picture. This is the design of that picture: where it lives, when
it is made, and why it is done this way rather than with object storage or an attachment.

## What the picture is

Every room keeps a png next to its artifact — `rooms/<room>/index.html` and
`rooms/<room>/index.png`. The png is the artifact rendered at the room's device (a width
and a height, sometimes rotated). It is not a cache: it is a deliverable, committed with
the room, and it is what a reviewer reads. `index.html` is the source the picture was
drawn from.

The device is the room's, not the project's: a kiosk, an admin PC and a phone in one
project each keep a snapshot that looks like the screen they are for. A room says which
in its frontmatter (`device: kiosk`); without one it uses `thumbnail.device`. The names,
widths, heights and rotation live in `modelroom.json` (or the built-ins `sp`, `tablet`,
`pc`). `docs/03-cli.md#snapshots` is the reference.

The room's outputs are therefore the docs (`BRIEF`, `SPEC`, `BEHAVIOUR`) and the snapshot.
The html sits between them: it produces the picture, but it is not what a review turns on.

## The decision

**Commit the png. A fixed name, overwritten in place. Squash and Merge on the way in.**

1. **Generated, then committed.** `modelroom render <room>` writes `index.png` next to the
   artifact. It is committed like any other room file.
2. **One fixed name.** Never `checkout-2026-10-20.png` or `checkout-v3.png`. The name is
   always `index.png`.
3. **Overwritten in place.** A render writes over the previous file. When the bytes do not
   change, nothing is written at all, so the commit only moves when the picture does. What
   that render drew from is recorded in local state (`.modelroom/state.json`, git-ignored)
   rather than in the png's timestamp — see *What "stale" means* below.
4. **Diffed by GitHub.** Because the path is stable, a pull request shows two versions of
   the same file under **Files changed**, with the image diff (Swipe / Onion Skin). That is
   the review surface.
5. **Squashed on merge.** The branch carries a binary per revision; a squash leaves main
   with a single current image, and git collects the intermediate blobs once the branch is
   gone.

## What each participant does

| | Does |
|---|---|
| `modelroom serve` | renders stale snapshots in the background, so the dashboard and the room show the current picture |
| `modelroom render` | the same, on demand and in CI (`--check` compares without writing) |
| the agent | reads the docs **and the picture**; commits the room's files together; opens the pull request |
| the reviewer | reads the picture in the pull request (and the docs and the BEHAVIOUR alongside it) |

modelroom renders and prints. It never touches git or `gh` — the branch, the commit and
the pull request belong to the agent, which already has them.

## What "stale" means

One definition, in `core/rooms.ts`: a room needs rendering when its artifact moved after
the last render, or a doc that names its device did. The artifact is the source of the
picture, and the device is part of what the picture is, so both date it.

The png's own mtime answers that question only when there is no record — a fresh checkout,
or a state file someone deleted. Normally there is one: every render, changed or not,
records the sources it drew from in `.modelroom/state.json`. That is what makes the promise
in point 3 work. A render that produces the same bytes must not touch the png, and if
staleness were read from the file's timestamp, that render would leave the room looking
stale forever — `serve` would render it again on the next change, and on the one after
that. The record is local and git-ignored on purpose: it says what *this machine* has
drawn, not something to commit.

## Why not the alternatives

**Object storage (S3, Cloudflare R2).** It removes the binary from the repository, but it
adds a service to run, credentials to hold, and — the decisive part — it puts design images
outside the machine that owns them. The tool stops being one command you can run anywhere.
An internal screen should not have to be uploaded to be reviewed.

**A base64 image in the pull request description.** GitHub caps a comment at 65,536
characters. A screen is far larger, so this cannot work for anything but a thumbnail.

**Renaming per revision.** Two files that are unrelated to GitHub is no diff at all — the
thing this design exists to produce.

**Committing without overwriting (keeping a history of images beside the artifact).** The
fixed name is what makes the diff; a directory of dated snapshots is a directory git cannot
compare.

## The one cost, and how it is paid

Binaries under version control grow a repository, because git keeps whole blobs and its
deltas are poor on already-compressed data. Here the growth is bounded three ways:

- **the fixed name** means one file per room, not one per revision;
- **idempotent rendering** means a commit only happens when the picture changes, and a
  render that changed nothing is remembered in local state instead of in the file;
- **Squash and Merge** means main keeps only the final image, and the revisions on the
  branch are pruned once it is deleted.

A repository that still feels large can put the snapshots behind **Git LFS**: add a
`.gitattributes` entry for `rooms/*/index.png` and let the image travel as a pointer. That
is a project decision, not a modelroom one — the tool works the same either way.

# DESIGN.md — the layer's design rules

Everything shared across the rooms lives here: the tokens, the components, the
accessibility floor. A room takes from this file and names what it took in its
`SPEC.md` (the `Uses:` line); it does not invent a colour, a type size or a button
that is already here. When two rooms would repeat the same decision, move it here
and reference it — do not copy it into both.

This file decides; two files carry. `design.css` at the layer root is the layer's own
CSS — the tokens and components below, written once and linked by every room. And when
the rooms are drawn with a real design system, `vendor/<system>/` holds its files,
copied once from the pinned package and committed. Neither is a room, and neither is
edited by hand. Keep this small: a design layer is not a component library. The tokens
below are the set `design.css` starts from; replace them with the project's own, once.

## The design system

Name the design system this layer draws from and where its truth lives, so an agent
knows what to read before writing markup:

- **Source:** (a package, a URL, a Figma file — wherever the components and tokens are defined)
- **Vendored:** (the pinned copy under `vendor/`, e.g. `vendor/bootstrap/` at version 5.3.8, or
  "none" while the layer uses only `design.css`)
- **MCP:** (the server's name, if an agent reads it through Model Context Protocol, or "none")

A room links the vendored copy and `design.css` relatively (`../../vendor/…`,
`../../design.css`), so the artifact renders from disk and is served under `/files/`. The copy
is refreshed by the project's script, not by an agent and not per room; implementation installs
the same version through its own dependency manager, and a room says which version it expects
in its `SPEC.md`.

An MCP server is *configured* in `opencode.json`, not here: OpenCode reads
`modelroom/opencode.json` because the agent runs from this directory. This file only
names which server matters, so the agent knows to use it; secrets stay in the
environment, never in either file.

## Tokens

A token is a CSS custom property, and this set lives in `design.css` — a room links that file
instead of carrying its own copy of the values.

```css
:root {
  --color-bg: #ffffff;
  --color-fg: #111827;
  --color-muted: #6b7280;
  --color-border: #e5e7eb;
  --color-accent: #2563eb;
  --color-danger: #b91c1c;

  --font: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
  --text-sm: 0.875rem;
  --text-md: 1rem;
  --text-lg: 1.25rem;
  --text-xl: 1.5rem;

  --space-1: 4px;
  --space-2: 8px;
  --space-3: 16px;
  --space-4: 24px;
  --space-5: 32px;

  --radius: 8px;
}
```

## Components

Anything two rooms share — a button, a field, a badge — is described here once: its
markup, its states, and the tokens it uses. The markup itself lives in `design.css`; a room
references it from its `SPEC.md`, and a room that needs a variation says so in its own
`SPEC.md` — it does not fork the component, and it does not restate it.

## Accessibility floor

- Contrast: body text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1); large text and UI, 3:1.
- Every interactive control is reachable and operable by keyboard alone.
- Focus is visible — never remove the outline without replacing it.
- A touch target is at least 44×44px wherever a finger is the input.

## What this file is not

- Not a room. A decision one screen needs belongs in that room's `SPEC.md`.
- Not the artifact. What can be seen in a screenshot belongs in `index.html`; this
  file holds the tokens the screen is drawn with, and the reasoning behind them.
- Not `design.css` or `vendor/`. Those are the shared files themselves — this is where
  their decisions are recorded, and `update` leaves this file alone.

# DESIGN.md — レイヤーのデザインルール

room をまたいで共有するものをここに置きます。トークン、コンポーネント、アクセシビリティの
下限です。room はこのファイルから取り、取ったものを `SPEC.md`（`使ってよいもの:` の行）に
書きます。ここにある色・文字サイズ・ボタンを room 側で作り直してはいけません。2つの room が
同じ判断を繰り返すなら、ここへ移して参照します — 両方にコピーしてはいけません。

決めるのはこのファイルで、持つのは2つのファイルです。レイヤーのルートにある `design.css` が
レイヤー自身の CSS で、下のトークンとコンポーネントを一度だけ書き、すべての room が
読み込みます。実際のデザインシステムから描く場合、`vendor/<system>/` にそのファイルを
置きます（固定したパッケージから一度だけコピーし、コミットしたもの）。どちらも room では
なく、手で編集するものでもありません。小さく保ってください。デザインレイヤーは
コンポーネントライブラリではありません。下のトークンは `design.css` の出発点です。
プロジェクト自身のものに一度だけ置き換えます。

## デザインシステム

このレイヤーがどのデザインシステムから描くのか、その正がどこにあるのかを書きます。agent は
マークアップを書く前に何を読むべきかを知れます。

- **正:**（パッケージ、URL、Figma ファイルなど、コンポーネントとトークンの定義がある場所）
- **ベンダリング:**（`vendor/` に固定して置いたコピー。例: `vendor/bootstrap/` の 5.3.8。
  `design.css` だけで描いている間は "none"）
- **MCP:**（agent が Model Context Protocol 経由で読む場合のサーバ名。なければ "none"）

room はベンダリングしたコピーと `design.css` を相対パス（`../../vendor/…`、
`../../design.css`）で読み込みます。そうすれば artifact はディスクから描画されるときも、
`/files/` 配下で配信されるときも同じように解決します。コピーの更新はプロジェクトの
スクリプトが行います — agent ではなく、room ごとでもありません。実装側は同じバージョンを
自分の依存管理で入れます。room は `SPEC.md` に、期待するバージョンを書きます。

MCP サーバの**設定**はここではなく `opencode.json` に書きます。agent はこのディレクトリで
動くので、OpenCode は `modelroom/opencode.json` を読みます。このファイルはどのサーバが
大事かを示すだけです。秘密情報は環境変数に置き、どちらのファイルにも書きません。

## トークン

トークンは CSS カスタムプロパティで、この一式は `design.css` に置きます — room は値のコピーを
持たず、そのファイルを読み込みます。

```css

  --color-bg: #ffffff;
  --color-fg: #111827;
  --color-muted: #6b7280;
  --color-border: #e5e7eb;
  --color-accent: #2563eb;
  --color-danger: #b91c1c;

  --font: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
  --text-sm: 0.875rem;
  --text-md: 1rem;
  --text-lg: 1.25rem;
  --text-xl: 1.5rem;

  --space-1: 4px;
  --space-2: 8px;
  --space-3: 16px;
  --space-4: 24px;
  --space-5: 32px;

  --radius: 8px;
}
```

## コンポーネント

2つの room が共有するもの — ボタン、入力欄、バッジ — はここに一度だけ書きます。マークアップ、
状態、使うトークンです。マークアップ自体は `design.css` に置き、room は `SPEC.md` からそれを
参照します。変化が要る room は、その `SPEC.md` にそう書きます。コンポーネントを分岐させず、
ここに書き直しもしません。

## アクセシビリティの下限

- コントラスト: 本文は WCAG AA（4.5:1）、大きい文字と UI は 3:1。
- すべての操作要素は、キーボードだけで到達・操作できる。
- フォーカスを見えるようにする — 代替なしに outline を消さない。
- 指で操作する場所では、タッチ対象は最低 44×44px。

## このファイルではないもの

- room ではありません。1画面だけが必要とする判断は、その room の `SPEC.md` に置きます。
- artifact ではありません。スクリーンショットで見えるものは `index.html` に属します。ここには
  画面を描くためのトークンと、その背景にある理由を置きます。
- `design.css` や `vendor/` ではありません。それらは共有されるファイルそのもので、ここは
  その判断を記録する場所です。`update` はこのファイルに触れません。
